title: SDK error messages and UX copybook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working copy of UX microcopy and behaviour patterns for SDK-visible errors across Redwood Inference client libraries (JS/TS, Python, Go). Goal: consistent, actionable, low-noise messages that help engineers recover quickly and reduce support tickets.

This doc focuses on:
- human-facing error text (CLI/console/logs/toasts)
- suggested developer UX patterns (retry, fallback, telemetry hints)
- short template examples per error class for each language surface
- policy notes for i18n/sensitive data and observability

Quick principles (working):
1) Be actionable: tell the developer what to do next (retry, check key, upgrade).
2) Prefer concise single-line summary + optional detail block for diagnostics.
3) Avoid leaking PII or payload content in copy, but include safe diagnostic tokens (request id).
4) Surface recovery options: automatic retry, fallback model, or sample code snippet.
5) Rate-limit and quota errors should contain clear next-steps and a link to billing/usage.
6) Keep tone professional, slightly helpful — not apologetic.

Error taxonomy (candidate):
- Auth: invalid API key, expired key, missing scopes
- Network: timeouts, DNS, TLS handshake fails
- Quota/RateLimit: per-minute, per-day, concurrent cap
- Model/Capacity: model-unavailable, overloaded, fallback triggered
- Validation: invalid param, schema mismatch, size too large
- Streaming: early-EOF, partial payload, WS disconnect
- Client bug: serialization, deserialization, runtime error in SDK logic
- Observability/Server: internal server error, degraded performance

Copy templates (single-line summary + optional detail):

Auth - invalid key (single-line):
"Authentication failed: invalid API key. Update REDWOOD_API_KEY and retry."

Auth - missing (detailed):
Summary: "API key not found.
"Details: \"No API key provided. Set environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass key to the client constructor. Request id: {request_id}.\"
Recovery hint: \"If you recently rotated keys, ensure your runtime has the new secret. See https://redwood.ai/docs/auth for examples.\"

Network - timeout (single-line):
"Request timed out. Retrying automatically (1/2) — still failing? Check connectivity or increase timeout."

Network - TLS failure (single-line):
"Secure connection failed: TLS handshake error. Verify system clock and root CA bundle."

Quota - rate limit (single-line):
"Rate limit exceeded. Slow down requests or request higher throughput from Billing. Retry after: {retry_after}s."

Quota - quota exceeded (detailed):
Summary: "Project quota reached: monthly token quota exhausted."
Detail: "Your project has consumed its monthly token quota. Contact billing@redwood.ai or use the Console to purchase additional capacity. Request id: {request_id}."

Model unavailable (single-line):
"Model currently unavailable in this region. We routed to fallback: {fallback_model}."

Validation - invalid param (single-line):
"Invalid input: field 'messages' must be an array of strings."

Streaming - partial (detailed):
Summary: "Streaming interrupted: partial output returned."
Detail: "We received a partial response. If you rely on streaming, retry from the last checkpoint or request a non-streaming call. Req id: {request_id}."

Internal server error (single-line):
"Something went wrong on our side (500). We're investigating — retry later. Provide request id {request_id} to support."

UX behavior patterns (recommended):
- CLI / SDK logs: single-line summary + JSON diagnostic object logged at DEBUG level (not shown to user by default). Provide request id in summary.
- Console/Playground UI: toast with single-line + CTA to view details (drawer) that includes sanitized diagnostics and suggested next steps.
- Automatic retries: network timeouts and 5xx -> exponential backoff (2 retries default). Auth errors -> immediate failure (do not retry). Quota -> fail fast with CTA.
- Fallbacks: if runtime routes to a fallback model, include explicit badge/notice with performance expectations (latency/cost) and option to pin to fallback or fail.
- Error telemetry: always attach stable request_id, sdk_version, region, model_id, and anonymized timing buckets. Avoid including prompt text or user PII in telemetry.

Examples (JS / Python snips for user-facing messages):
JS (pseudo):
try {
  await client.generate(...);
} catch (err) {
  // user-friendly message
  console.error('Generation failed: ' + err.userMessage || 'See logs for details');
  // for support: include request id if present
  if (err.request_id) console.info('Request id:', err.request_id);
}

Python (pseudo):
try:
    resp = client.generate(...)
except RedwoodAuthError as e:
    print('Authentication failed: check REDWOOD_API_KEY')
    logging.debug('auth error details: %s', e)

Checklists for implementers (SDK authors):
- [ ] Implement Error class hierarchy with fields: code, userMessage, request_id, retry_after (optional), details (only for debug).
- [ ] Default userMessage must be localized via i18n service; English fallback required.
- [ ] Map HTTP status -> SDK error code (401->Auth, 429->RateLimit, 504->Timeout, 500->Server).
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks for request_id and sdk_version; redact prompt/inputs by default.
- [ ] Provide a dev-mode opt-in: show full diagnostic block in console when REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How much diagnostic detail is acceptable in default logs vs debug mode? (privacy + support efficiency)
- Should SDKs expose a uniform retry policy or let app teams opt entirely? Proposal: sensible default with opt-out.
- i18n: who will own translations? product content or i18n infra team? Need budget for top 6 locales.
- Should rate limit messages include link to tenant-specific usage page (requires Console integration)?

Localization & accessibility notes:
- Keep messages short for screen readers; avoid punctuation-heavy lines.
- Provide aria-live regions for toasts; ensure focus management when showing modals for blocking errors.
- Use plain language, avoid internal jargon (e.g., use 'quota' not 'commit' for public-facing).

Next steps (action items):
- Share with SDK leads (Mar 10) for feedback on proposed Error API.
- Prototype JS SDK behavior with automatic retry + userMessage surface (owner: Marcus).
- Add a Playground demo that intentionally triggers each class of error for documentation and e2e tests (owner: Sofia).
- Create ticket in Jira: DX-342 to track i18n and Console links.

Notes / scratch lines:
- Consider adding short micro-copy for 'silent' telemetry consent in enterprise/private deployments.
- Keep a central canonical mapping table in repo: docs/errors.md (linked to SDK READMEs).

References and examples used while drafting:
- Stripe API error patterns (inspiration): precise codes + helpful links
- Cloud provider consoles: clear quota CTAs
- Previous internal ticket: jira DX-117 (support load from unclear error messages)

End of draft.

(If you edit: update last_modified and add short changelog at top.)
